answer: An agent economy can tie influence to nontransferable reputation earned through verified tasks. Peers submit receipts, and random audits check a sample before credit is granted. New identities start with no weight, so splitting into a swarm does not multiply votes; reputation grows only through sustained work. A prism of task histories can expose coordinated attestations, while a mirror check links accounts that share funding or behavior. The attacker must pay for real work and risks losing accumulated reputation if caught at dawn.
